paper_metadata.title: Quantum Computing for Multi Period Asset Allocation

summary: The paper presents a gate-based IBM Quantum System One study of multi-period, multi-asset portfolio simulation using 9 qubits for a [3,3,3] asset encoding, with 120 shots per execution and 20 years of historical market data to estimate covariance. It reports that [3,3,3] circuits built in a few seconds, [4,4,4] took about 30 seconds on hardware, and [5,5,5] failed after roughly 6 minutes, while the authors compare input/output covariance matrices but do not demonstrate classical speedup.

experiments.description: Quantum simulation of multi-period multi-asset portfolio returns using a gate-based IBM Quantum System One circuit to generate multivariate normal-distributed monthly returns and evaluate rebalancing rules.

algorithm.variant: Quantum circuit for multivariate normal distribution / portfolio return simulation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 3 qubits allocated per asset class, giving a qubit array of [3,3,3]; a quantum circuit is generated for a discretized multivariate normal distribution over returns and then combined for the three assets.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Generate monthly return samples from a multivariate log-normal / multivariate normal approximation using historical covariance and expected returns, then use the simulated returns to assess portfolio rebalancing performance.

problem_instance.description: Multi-asset, multi-period asset allocation for a 3-asset portfolio.
problem_instance.dataset_name: S&P 500, MSCI All Country World Index ex US, Bloomberg Global Aggregate indices

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Historical data used to compute volatilities and covariance matrix; expected returns set to 10%, 10%, and 6%.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute volatilities and covariance matrix from 20 years of historical index data; assume multivariate log-normal distribution and monthly sampling; set distribution bounds to ±3 standard deviations around expected returns.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare input and output covariance matrices to assess simulation error; run portfolio simulations under monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual rebalancing rules.

hardware.device_name: IBM Quantum System One / ibm_rensselaer (IBM Quantum Eagle processor, 127 qubits)

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Historical covariance and expected returns computed classically from market data; simulator used before running on hardware.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert measured qubit outcomes into returns and compare covariance matrices; evaluate rebalancing performance.
implementation_details.circuit_compilation_time: [3,3,3] built within a few seconds on emulator and on physical quantum computer; [4,4,4] took ~30 seconds on hardware; [5,5,5] failed after ~6 minutes on hardware.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not claim or demonstrate a classical speedup. It states the problem is classically solvable and focuses on feasibility/software development. Hardware build-time limitations are reported instead of speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 9 qubits on IBM Quantum System One / ibm_rensselaer, with 120 shots per execution; simulator and hardware runs reported for [3,3,3], [4,4,4], and [5,5,5] qubit arrays.
limiting_factors: No classical baseline performance is reported for the same task
